extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers of rOpenSci R package submissions (rOpenSci software peer-review)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting, submitting, and following up on reviews of R packages submitted to rOpenSci, including procedural steps, checklist items, tooling, and interpersonal expectations. Focused on reviewers who will assess code, documentation, tests, CI, and package structure on GitHub.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review timeliness and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Please strive to complete your review within 3 weeks of accepting a review request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will aim to remind reviewers of upcoming and past due dates. Editors may assign additional or alternate reviewers if a review is excessively late. Contact the editor directly or in the submission thread to inform them about possible delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respectfulness and code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be open, non-adversarial, and focused on improving software quality. Be respectful and kind!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rOpenSci code of conduct is mandatory for everyone involved in the review process. Provide constructive feedback and follow community norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the review template as primary checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin by copying the rOpenSci review template and using it as a high-level checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to checking off minimum criteria, provide general comments addressing the listed package questions (see separate criteria). The review template organizes the review workflow and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base review on the correct GitHub branch
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be based on the latest GitHub version on the default branch, unless otherwise indicated by package authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the package is not submitted via the default/main branch, switch to the submitted review branch before starting your review. GitHub search is limited to the default branch, so you may need to search the package locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check the pkgcheck / initial package report
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions trigger a detailed report on package structure and functionality generated by the rOpenSci pkgcheck package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect the initial package report generated by @ropensci-review-bot. If the package has changed substantially since the last checks, request a re-check with the comment: @ropensci-review-bot check package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure installation dependencies are present
rubrics_metrics.description: When installing the package to review it, make sure you have all dependencies available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For instance, run pak::pak() to install dependencies before testing or checking the package locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: rOpenSci packaging guide compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the package comply with the rOpenSci packaging guide?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the packaging guide as a baseline for structural and policy expectations; flag deviations and suggest fixes where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code style and code patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there improvements that could be made to the code style and to code patterns?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: do functions need to be broken down into smaller helper functions and is the role of each helper function clear? Provide concrete suggestions for refactoring and style improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce code duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there code duplication in the package that should be reduced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out duplicated logic and recommend consolidation into reusable functions or modules to improve maintainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reinventing functionality available in base or lightweight deps
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there functions in base R or lightweight dependencies that provide the same interface as some helper functions in the package?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify opportunities to rely on well-tested existing implementations rather than reimplementing functionality; this may simplify the package and reduce maintenance burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: User interface / API ergonomics
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there user interface improvements that could be made?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider function names, argument order/defaults, clarity of return values, and whether the API is intuitive for target users. Aim for a logical programming API that is easy to read and autocompletable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there performance improvements that could be made?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify hotspots, offer alternatives (vectorization, algorithms, caching), and suggest benchmarks or tests to demonstrate improvements where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation clarity and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the documentation (installation instructions/vignettes/examples/demos) clear and sufficient?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does it use the principle of multiple points of entry (i.e., any piece of documentation may be the first encounter the user has with the package)? Check vignettes, README, examples, and demos for completeness and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming consistency for API and autocomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: Were functions and arguments named to work together to form a common, logical programming API that is easy to read, and autocomplete?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess naming patterns, consistency across functions, and whether naming aids discoverability via editor autocomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise the package with real use-cases
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have your own relevant data/problem, work through it with the package to find rough edges and use-cases the author didn’t think about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Playing the 'naive user' role can surface UX issues; ask 'What did I think this thing would do? Does it do it? What are the things that scare me off?'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use automated tools and CI logs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use automated tools to facilitate your review: check initial package report, CI logs, and run checks/tests locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested actions: inspect @ropensci-review-bot report, check the package’s logs on CI services (GitHub Actions, Codecov, etc.), run devtools::check() and devtools::test() locally to find errors that may not appear on the author’s system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify test skipping is justified
rubrics_metrics.description: See whether tests’ skipping is justified (e.g., skip_on_cran tests that do real API requests vs. skipping all tests on one operating system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure any skipped tests have clear, justifiable reasons and that skipping doesn't mask real failures or reduce test coverage inappropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect documentation hosted on pkgdown carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation hosted on a pkgdown website is not necessarily up-to-date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend inspecting the package’s documentation locally by running pkgdown::build_site() to ensure docs reflect the current branch and code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture off-thread interactions in the review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you interact with package authors outside a review thread (chats, DMs, in-person, issues in the project repo), make sure your review captures and/or links to relevant elements from those conversations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include links or text from off-thread discussions so the review thread remains a centralized record of decisions and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting the review to the software-review issue
rubrics_metrics.description: When your review is complete, paste it as a comment into the package software-review issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional comments are welcome in the same issue. Package reviews are intended as an ongoing conversation rather than a single round. If you create issues or pull requests on the package repo, comment about them and link to them in the software-review thread so there's a centralized record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include time estimate for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Please include an estimate of how many hours you spent on your review afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add this time estimate to your review comment in the software-review issue to help the project track reviewer effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review follow-up and change verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should respond within 2 weeks with changes to the package in response to your review; reviewers should respond whether the changes sufficiently address issues raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage ongoing discussion between authors and reviewers; ask editors to clarify issues in the review thread as needed. Use the approval template when approving changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteering etiquette and process
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to volunteer as a reviewer, fill the volunteering form and follow the guidance about volunteering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see a submission relevant to your interests, email [email protected] with package name, submission issue URL, and assigned editor. Do not volunteer for all issues, and do not volunteer via the GitHub interface. Reviewer invitations are at the editor’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pkgreviewr helper package to streamline review workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: If working in RStudio, you can streamline your review workflow by using the pkgreviewr package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installation and usage example provided (remotes::install_github('ropensci-org/pkgreviewr'); pkgreview_create(...)) — it clones the package repo and creates a review project with a notebook and the review template. Note: if reviewing a non-default branch, switch branches after cloning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regenerating package check results during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may re-generate package check results from @ropensci-review-bot at any time by issuing a single comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the comment: @ropensci-review-bot check package to request a fresh package report during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit rOpenSci when reusing standards elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use rOpenSci standards/checklists when reviewing software elsewhere, tell the recipients that they came from rOpenSci and inform rOpenSci publicly or by email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share provenance: tell journal editors, students, or internal code review recipients that the standards originated from rOpenSci and notify rOpenSci via their public forum or email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from example reviews and reviewer experience
rubrics_metrics.description: First-time reviewers may benefit from reading past submission threads and reviewer blog posts to understand expected review depth and style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and blog posts are linked; reviewers do not need to write reviews as long as some examples, but can use them to structure their own feedback. Consider alternating between using the package and inspecting code (as described by experienced reviewers).
